title: Polish president's aide urges PM to "find the courage" to formally strip Zelenskyy of Poland's highest honour
text:
Долучайтеся до клубу УП!

Zbigniew Bogucki, Head of the Chancellery of the President of Poland Karol Nawrocki, has called on Prime Minister Donald Tusk to "find the courage" to sign the decision formally stripping Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of the Order of the White Eagle, Poland's highest state honour.

Source: Bogucki on X (Twitter), as reported by European Pravda

Details: Most of Bogucki's post criticised Tusk over the appointment of judges, but he concluded by referring to the earlier controversy surrounding the decision to revoke the Polish state honour awarded to the Ukrainian president.

Quote: "Instead of putting meaningless signatures on documents appointing judicial assessors, which have always required only the signature of the president of the Republic of Poland, I urge you to find the courage to fulfil your duty and finally sign the presidential decision to strip the president of Ukraine of the Order of the White Eagle."

Details: It is noted that when President Karol Nawrocki decided to revoke Zelenskyy's Order of the White Eagle, the decision also required Donald Tusk's signature. However, the Ukrainian president returned the decoration before that procedure was completed.
